messages.subject: Waiting for multiple batches to arrive at a resource
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to simulate a process where batch1 seizes a resource but depending on attribute1 value it branches either to have a timeout(10) and release resource or waits for a signal that batch2 has seized resource and then continues the path (timeout(10)) and batch 1 and 2 leave resource together. 

Is this possible?

I tried it below, however the problem I am having is when the signal is triggered and it waits for batch 2 to arrive at resource and processes with timeout(10) it doesn't log batch 1 leaving the resource, only batch 2. Batch 1 disappears after it enters resource. Any reason why?

Signaler_1<-trajectory()%>%
  timeout(time until next batch reaches resource)%>%
  send(signal)

processing<-trajectory()%>%
  branch(function()get_attribute(env,"attribute1")<70,
         continue=TRUE,
         trajectory()%>%
           trap(signal)%>%
           log_("waiting for new batch")%>%
           wait()%>%
           untrap(signal)
         
  )%>%
  timeout(20) #processing time



seize("resource")%>%
  log_("Enters resource")%>%
  set_attribute("attribute1", function()
    sample(50:99,1))%>%
  log_(function()
    paste0(get_attribute(env, "attribute1"), "% attribute1"))%>%
  join(processing)%>%
  release("resource")%>%
  log_("Leaves resource")


  add_resource("resource", capacity=Inf)%>%


Thanks

Shereen

There's a "name" argument to the batch activity, but then you lose the
numbers, i.e., the distinction among batches under the same name.
However, note that batch identifiers are merely informational and only
appear in logs or debugging information (verbose=TRUE): they are NOT
monitored. Batches are "fictitious" entities, so only arrivals are
monitored. I suggest you to rely on them, not on batches.

So 10 arrivals seize resource for a timeout period and all 10 release resource at same time?

On Monday, November 6, 2017 at 12:24:22 PM UTC, Shereen Ashraf wrote:
Hi,

I am trying to simulate a process where batch1 seizes a resource but depending on attribute1 value it branches either to have a timeout(10) and release resource or waits for a signal that batch2 has seized resource and then continues the path (timeout(10)) and batch 1 and 2 leave resource together. 

Is this possible?

I tried it below, however the problem I am having is when the signal is triggered and it waits for batch 2 to arrive at resource and processes with timeout(10) it doesn't log batch 1 leaving the resource, only batch 2. Batch 1 disappears after it enters resource. Any reason why?

Signaler_1<-trajectory()%>%

  send(signal)

  branch(function()get_attribute(env,"attribute1")<70,

         trajectory()%>%
           trap(signal)%>%

    paste0(get_attribute(env, "attribute1"), "% attribute1"))%>%
  join(processing)%>%
  release("resource")%>%
  log_("Leaves resource")


  add_resource("resource", capacity=Inf)%>%
